segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Dana. I wanted to confirm the updated seat count and make sure the order form lines up with your June 3 go-live.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Sure. We’re at 42 full seats and 18 read-only. That includes the finance team and the two regional managers we added last week.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Got it, 42 full and 18 read-only. I have that in the CRM now. On pricing, that puts the annual subscription at $38,640, and implementation is the one-time $6,500 we discussed.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay, that matches my notes. Can you make sure the invoice is split? Our controller wants subscription billed now and services billed after kickoff.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, that’s fine. I’ll note subscription due on signature and implementation invoiced after the May 20 kickoff. Payment terms are net 30, same as the draft.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Net 30 works. One thing, our legal team asked about the renewal notice. The draft says 60 days. Can we make that 30?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, so I can approve 30 days without going back through deal desk. I’ll update that clause and send the clean version this afternoon.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. If we get it by 3, I can route it for signature today. Our CFO is out Friday, so I’d like to catch him before then.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Understood. I’ll send the revised order form and the invoice split note by 2:30 Eastern. Once it’s signed, we’ll introduce your implementation lead and lock the May 20 kickoff.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Sounds good. Send it to me and copy Marcus in procurement. He’s the one who’ll generate the PO.
